name: community_handshake_states
description: One row per attempt to establish a trusted channel with another community. It is the state machine behind server/federation/authentication.json, written down so a restart does not lose a handshake in flight.

columns.name: handshake_id
columns.description: The identifier both sides carry through the exchange. Not this row's id — the other community chose it.

columns.name: one_time_code
columns.description: The code sent back over the callback to prove the caller is who it claimed. Single use.

columns.name: public_key
columns.description: The key of the community on the other end.

columns.name: api_version
columns.note: Legacy declares 255 here and 10 on federated_communities.api_version for the same values. gradido2 should use one width; 10 is the one that fits.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.description: Touched on every state change. A row whose updated_at is older than FEDERATION_AUTHENTICATION_TIMEOUT_MS is EXPIRED whatever its status says.

notes: The status column has no name in legacy's @Column decorator, so TypeORM's default applies and the column is literally `status`. Confirmed against migration 0095.

EXPIRED is derived, not written by a timer: an implementation that only reads the status and never compares updated_at against FEDERATION_AUTHENTICATION_TIMEOUT_MS will keep answering a handshake that timed out ten minutes ago. Both implementations must apply the timeout on read.
one_time_code is a bearer secret for the length of one handshake. Never logged, never returned. See logging.json.
Timestamps are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json.
